about: Known limits of check-all's Gate 0 rows (port/tools/check_all.py, KNOWN_LIMITS; port/test/README.md, "Known limits of check-all rows"). A row listed here whose compare is DIFFERENT only inside its limits' windows (field: [[first, last], ...] ticks of compare.json's result.ticks_per_field; "sequence": the lag replay's off ticks; "sram": [[first, last], ...] SRAM offsets the end-SRAM compare may differ in) is KNOWN, not FAIL; anything outside them fails as before. Every entry is a recorded limit of the test tool or a recorded kind, never a port difference left unfixed.

route-br9-lag.kind: the lag replay's limit, C10-10 (c)'s kind: GBA lag VBlanks inside a BIOS LZ77 decompression (DIVERGENCES section 5, Lag check v2, not resolved; coverage 11's N-C11-1, integration 11's choice 4)
route-br9-lag.note: Lagdou Ruins floor 9, turn 15: palette 9 colours 12-15 (the map's flickering palette) one step out of order after 4 GBA lag VBlanks inside an LZ77 decompression into VRAM, 62,549-62,563 (pending/c11-findings.md 2a); the same four colours again at the change to floor 10, 96,999-97,215 (GBA lag ticks 96,999 and 97,000: the GBA holds the new map's colours, the PC run the flicker's first entry; inferred the same kind, not probed: pending/c12-findings.md); every other field equal, no frame differs

route-br9-lag.kind: the GBA reference's DMA open-bus timing (mGBA GBALoadBad): D-60's NULL-unit pid reads in PidStatsRecordTargetListDefeats (0x08026448/0x08026454) return a DMA bus value when a DMA stalled the CPU there, so the GBA writes BWL records for real pids; the value depends on cycle timing (an extra breakpoint flips it), which the PC does not model (port-plan/pending/fix-bwl.md)
route-br9-lag.note: tick 94,747: GBA PidStatsRecordLoseData(7) (lossAmt 1 to 2, favval -0x80) in suspend.0, suspend.1 and game.0

route-er3-lag.kind: the lag replay's placement after a Proc_Start (C10-10 (c)'s kind), then the proc-slot knock-on and a retail uninitialised read (DIVERGENCES section 5, Knock-on: proc slot order)
route-er3-lag.note: Lagdou Ruins floor 3 with the real army: a GBA lag VBlank in efxExcalibur_Loop_Main's step runs after efxExcaliburBGCOL3's Proc_Start on the PC run (46,646), so that proc takes another slot; at four later phase changes TerrainDisplay_Loop_OnSideChange reads another leftover windowQuadrant from the recycled slot (src/player_interface.c:1154, retail), the map's side windows slide in a tick apart (BG0/BG1 3 ticks, the main-loop events 45 against 44); every game value equal (pending/c12-postgame-real.md)

route-gallery-lag.kind: the lag replay's placement after a Proc_Start (C10-10 (c)'s kind, H-c12-pr-1's), then the proc-slot knock-on and a retail uninitialised read (DIVERGENCES section 5, Knock-on: proc slot order)
route-gallery-lag.note: The item gallery (cheat-assisted), P-41: Excalibur's battle animation at tick 93,316: the GBA's lag VBlank (lag_at 19) came after efxExcalibur's sub-proc start at event 19 and before the next Proc_Start's AllocateProcess, and its OnVBlank freed proc slot 56, which that Proc_Start then took; the lag replay runs it at event 20 (the new proc's RunProcessScript entry), after AllocateProcess took slot 15 (GBA probe on AllocateProcess 0x08002D84 and FreeProcess 0x08002D94; the PC's -finstrument-functions hooks), so sProcAllocList differs from 93,316 on. At turns 21-26 the cursor rests on a unit and TerrainDisplay's step reads leftover proc-slot data (src/player_interface.c, retail): at 94,511 and 104,696 the PC run's gProcScr_TerrainDisplay step makes a VRAM copy to 0x06001000 that the GBA's step does not make at that tick (one main-loop event more), so the side windows' BG0/BG1 cells differ for 1-4 ticks and frame 104,700 with them; every game value equal (pending/r13-fixes.md)

route-gallery-lag.kind: a frame on a GBA lag tick, every traced field equal (round 8's kind 2, c10 F-E2-2; port/test/README.md, Raster-timing frames, Not covered): the lag replay runs a GBA lag VBlank, and that lag frame's lines, at an event boundary, where the GBA's came inside a step
route-gallery-lag.note: The item gallery (cheat-assisted), C12-GAL-6, measured in fix round 14 from the c12-gallery photos with every frame (pending/r14-fixes.md). Each frame is on a GBA lag tick and is the only difference. Recover 127,456 and Physic 130,087: the step that ends src/bb.c's bottom-bar HBlank handler (SetPrimaryHBlankHandler(NULL), REG_IE 0x2003 -> 0x2001) ran on the GBA while its last lag frame drew lines 140-159, so the handler's last write left REG_BLDCNT 0x00EC with the bar's REG_BLDY and the tick's frame is darkened on every line until the next flush; the lag replay runs that lag frame's lines after the step (the handler already off); at Physic's lag VBlank the GBA's gLCDControlBuffer is half-written (BLDCNT 0x38C4, the PC's 0x38C8 with BLDY 4). Gleipnir 120,882/888/894, Naglfar 129,436-129,448 and 129,488-129,492, Ivaldi 27,278: the tree-0 palette copy at the GBA's lag VBlank (lag_at 25, 19, 37) used the step's state before it finished (gPaletteBuffer FNV-1a: Gleipnir GBA 1743820e, PC 17798ed6; Naglfar GBA d4ec7a83, PC 6a32fed5; Ivaldi equal, another input), so the PC's frame shows the GBA's next frame's palette (Ivaldi: PLTT after the lag VBlank GBA d6a16817, PC 1c7384b7 = the GBA's frame 27,279). Only an every-frame run shows these (the CHECK_LONG row samples frames).
